AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JULY 5, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  5:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk City Employees Association.

  II.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk Association of Management Employees.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Property: 12700 Norwalk Boulevard; Negotiating Parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager,
  on behalf of the City and Primestor Development Inc.; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

  IV.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Property: Assessor Property Numbers 8056-015-014 and 8056-025-020; Negotiating
  Parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager, on behalf of the City and Primestor Development Inc.; Under
  Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Pastor Jacob Mathews
  Rock of the Nations Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Leah Mendez, 8th grader
  Lakeside Middle School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS
  City Council to present the 2022 City of Norwalk Environmental Awareness Scholarships.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Coffee with a Cop recap.

  3.  Independence Day Festival highlights.
   4.  Department Highlights – Finance.

  5.  Bi-Weekly Review.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of June 21,
  2022. 825-04

  Minutes

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period June 12, 2022 – June
  25, 2022, in the total amount of $1,088,951.33. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period June
  14, through June 27, 2022 in the total amount of $1,997,201. 640

  Warrant Register

  5.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-38 - DESTRUCTION OF OBSOLETE RECORDS – ADMINISTRATION AND
  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENTS - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution
  No. 22-38, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING
  THE DESTRUCTION OF CERTAIN RECORDS IN THE ADMINISTRATION AND COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENTS. 870-02

  Report

  6.  REMOVAL OF ADVISORY BODY MEMBER – It is respectfully requested that City Council affirm my
  request to remove Mr. Ramirez from the Historical Heritage Commission effective immediately. 235

  Report

  7.  AGREEMENT – LEGISLATIVE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM – Staff recommends City Council approve
  an agreement with Prime Government Solutions, Inc. to provide automated agenda management and
  video display software and support effective July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2025, in the amount of
  $39,186 for year one, $32,971 in year two and annual renewals with five percent increase thereafter;
  and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments provided there is
  funding in budget and it is within the City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form
  approved by the City Attorney. 825

  Report

  8.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 1 - PUBLIC AFFAIRS AND COMMUNICATION SERVICES - Staff
  recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 1 to the agreement with Merino, Barajas &
  Associates, Inc. not to exceed $36,000 from July 1, 2022 to October 31, 2022; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute this amendment on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.
  710-07

  Report

  9.  ORDINANCE NO. 22-1732 AMENDING TITLE 8 (HEALTH AND SAFETY), CHAPTER 8.52 (WATER
  CONSERVATION REQUIREMENTS) OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO ALIGN WITH THE
  STATE’S EMERGENCY WATER USE REGULATIONS AND PHASE II OF THE NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL WATER SYSTEM’S WATER SHORTAGE CONTINGENCY PLAN - Staff recommends City
   Council accept for second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 22-1732, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  OF NORWALK, AMENDING CHAPTER 8.52 OF TITLE 8, OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  ALIGN WITH THE STATE’S EMERGENCY WATER USE REGULATIONS AND PHASE II OF THE
  NORWALK MUNICIPAL WATER SYSTEM’S WATER SHORTAGE CONTINGENCY PLAN. 1070-03

  Report

  10. ACCEPT WORK FOR CITYWIDE ANNUAL SIDEWALK/CONCRETE REPAIR AND REPLACEMENT
  PROJECT NO. 3302-2122 – ENGINEERS REPORT 22-10 - Staff recommends the City Council accept
  the work of Towo Enterprise, Inc. in the amount of $386,059 for citywide annual sidewalk/concrete
  repair and replacement and curb ramp installations to comply with Americans with Disabilities Act
  standards. 1005-04-3302-2122

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  11. ADVISORY BODIES - Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

RESOLUTIONS

  12. RESOLUTION NO. 22-39 - NORWALK CITY EMPLOYEES ASSOCIATION MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING AND RESOLUTION NO. 22-40 - APPROVING A REVISED FISCAL YEAR 2022/23
  SALARY SCHEDULE - Staff recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  Resolution No. 22-39, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  APPROVING THE MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AND THE NORWALK CITY EMPLOYEES ASSOCIATION - GENERAL AND HOURLY UNITS; and

  b.  Resolution No. 22-40, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  AMENDING THE SALARY SCHEDULE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022-2025 FOR THE
  GENERAL,HOURLY,  AND  EXECUTIVE  MANAGEMENT  AND  MID-MANAGEMENT
  EMPLOYEES. 135-09

  Report

REPORTS

  13. ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT UPDATE – Oral presentation to be provided for information. No action
  is required. 1400

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING

  14. APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S DENIAL OF PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN 2035
  AND CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT NO. 1026 – 11042 ROSECRANS AVENUE – RESOLUTION NO.
  22-37 - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-37, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK SETTING FORTH ITS FINDINGS OF FACT AND DECISION
  RELATIVE TO THE DENIAL OF PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 2035 AND CONDITIONAL
  USE PERMIT NO. 1026. 320-01-1026/320-04-2035

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated July 1, 2022.
 Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
